semantics: Selects schedule-iteration algorithm #1 (the 'do half the local reads first' simple scheduler) inside _makeSubIterSchedule. The function-local `scheduleIterAlg` is seeded from self.states.scheduleIterAlg (== kernel["_ScheduleIterAlg"], the remap of the ScheduleIterAlg enum; value 4 -> 0) at line 877, then FORCED to 0 when (NLLlast and tailloopInNll) at lines 878-880. The elif at 951 fires iff the resulting value == 1. self.states.scheduleIterAlg itself is 0 unless KernelLanguage selects the Assembly path (lines 6243 vs 6247).

scheduleIterAlg.note: function-local int derived from kernel["_ScheduleIterAlg"]; ScheduleIterAlg YAML/CLI enum is [0,1,2,3,4] with 4 remapped to 0 (Solution.py:599). Domain [0,1,2,3] covers True(1) and False(0,2,3).

KernelLanguage.note: ValidParameters.py:915 - only valid value. On non-Assembly path states.scheduleIterAlg is pinned 0 (line 6247), so pred would be always-False; not in scope.

NLLlast.note: ASSUMPTION knob: live loop/codegen state. When (NLLlast and tailloopInNll) the local value is forced to 0, making pred False regardless of the config enum.

tailloopInNll.note: ASSUMPTION knob: live loop/codegen state (see NLLlast).

encoding.method: Integer variable scheduleIterAlg constrained to {0,1,2,3}; predicate = (scheduleIterAlg == 1). The runtime override is modeled in the pure_helper as eff = 0 if (nll_last and tailloop_in_nll) else schedule_iter_alg, then eff == 1.
encoding.note: Core branch is a single integer == comparison over a finite enum -> fully tractable in z3. The NLLlast/tailloopInNll force-to-0 override is the only non-config dependency; it is an upstream guard, not part of the 951 comparison itself.

true_examples.reason: config _ScheduleIterAlg=1 and no NLL force-to-0 -> local scheduleIterAlg==1 -> elif fires (schedule alg #1)

false_examples.reason: _ScheduleIterAlg=0 -> handled by the if at line 882, elif skipped
_ScheduleIterAlg=2 -> falls through to elif at line 998
config is 1 but (NLLlast and tailloopInNll) forces local value to 0 at line 880 -> pred False (assumption-dependent)

pure_helper:
def schedule_iter_alg_is_one(schedule_iter_alg: int, nll_last: bool, tailloop_in_nll: bool) -> bool:
    """Pure model of KernelWriter.py:951 predicate `scheduleIterAlg == 1`.
    Mirrors lines 877-880: local scheduleIterAlg seeded from kernel[\"_ScheduleIterAlg\"]
    (enum in {0,1,2,3}) but FORCED to 0 when (NLLlast and tailloopInNll). Branch fires iff ==1.
    pre: 0 <= schedule_iter_alg <= 3
    post: __return__ == ((0 if (nll_last and tailloop_in_nll) else schedule_iter_alg) == 1)
    """
    eff = 0 if (nll_last and tailloop_in_nll) else schedule_iter_alg
    return eff == 1

crosshair.caveat: CrossHair: absence of a counterexample is NOT a proof of correctness.

notes: z3 4.16.0 actually executed in-container; TRUE witness scheduleIterAlg=1, FALSE witness scheduleIterAlg=0; full-domain partition {1} true / {0,2,3} false; agrees with python reference.

classification = solver-backed-under-assumptions: the 951 comparison itself is a pure finite-enum integer ==, fully solvable; but the EFFECTIVE value can be overridden to 0 by the (NLLlast and tailloopInNll) live-loop guard at 878-880, and the enum is only non-zero on the Assembly KernelLanguage path (line 6243). Witnesses are valid under the stated assumptions (Assembly path, override not firing).
Reachability: also gated by the if-chain order (if==0 at 882 handles 0; this elif only reached when scheduleIterAlg != 0).
ScheduleIterAlg config value 4 is remapped to 0 (_ScheduleIterAlg), so user value 4 makes this predicate False, same as 0.
